feed.title: Verizon Waives Charges for Hurricane Lowell, Prepares Network in Hawai'i
feed.summary: Verizon is waiving domestic call, text, and data charges for customers on Kaua’i through September 14 due to Major Hurricane Lowell. The company has also reinforced its network infrastructure in Hawai'i with backup generators, satellite assets, and pre-staged equipment, and is collaborating with emergency management to ensure connectivity. Verizon is urging residents and businesses to take digital preparedness steps, such as charging devices, securing backups, and establishing communication plans.

feed.title: Uber and city near Mount Fuji join hands in measures against overtourism
feed.summary: Uber's Japanese unit has partnered with Fujiyoshida city near Mount Fuji to combat overtourism issues like traffic congestion and littering. This first-of-its-kind agreement with a Japanese municipality will involve Uber setting up designated pickup spots away from crowded areas and using its app to inform tourists about local customs and etiquette. The initiative aims to balance tourism growth with the well-being of local residents.

feed.title: Maryland bills could rise 5.3% under a Potomac Edison plan. Rates would still be lowest among investor-owned utilities.
feed.summary: Potomac Edison has proposed a $52.8 million rate adjustment in Maryland to fund upgrades to its electric system, which would result in an average residential customer bill increase of about 5.3%. Despite this potential increase, the company asserts that its residential rates would remain the lowest among Maryland's investor-owned utilities, being 25% below the in-state peer average as of June 1. The proposal, which aims to strengthen reliability through grid modernization, infrastructure improvements, and expanded tree-clearing, requires review and approval by the Maryland Public Service Commission.

feed.title: Boycott of Starbucks Is Still On as Workers Press for $17 Wage and Protections
feed.summary: Starbucks Workers United is continuing its boycott of the coffee giant this Labor Day weekend, demanding a minimum hourly wage of $17, improved staffing, and better workplace protections. This ongoing action follows a recent victory where Starbucks stopped using a silica-based powder in its drinks due to worker complaints. The union faces challenges from a Republican-majority National Labor Relations Board, which has overturned several pro-union rulings.
